title: Bounded resolutions by finite projectives over a Noetherian ring
statement: Let R be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], M a finitely generated R-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and d a natural number. If Ext_R^i(M,N) [def-pc-ext] vanishes for every module N and every i>d, then M has a projective resolution [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] with finite terms [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and all terms of degree greater than d zero. Projectivity has the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

source.place: Tags 00O4, 00O5, 0CXE and 065R; bounded-projective model and finite-resolution arguments

proof.text: Induct on d. At d=0 the Mathlib equivalence projective_iff_hasProjectiveDimensionLE_zero makes M projective. Its identity resolution has M in degree zero and zero elsewhere, all finite.

At d+1 use Module.exists_finite_presentation to choose a finite free module F surjecting onto M. Its kernel K is finite by Noetherianity. Mathlib ShortExact.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_X₃_iff gives the Ext bound d for K. Apply induction.

Augment the chosen resolution Q of K by F as degree zero and by F→M as augmentation. The first new differential is Q₀→K→F. Exactness in degree zero follows from surjectivity of Q₀→K and exactness of K→F→M; degree one uses injectivity of K→F and exactness of Q₁→Q₀→K. Higher exactness is that of Q. The exact-and-epi quasi-isomorphism criterion supplies a ProjectiveResolution. Its terms are F and the terms of Q, so they are finite and projective, and vanish above d+1.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_bounded_finite_projective_resolution
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) [Module.Finite R M] (d : ℕ)
    (h : HasProjectiveDimensionLE M d) :
    ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution M,
      (∀ i : ℕ, Module.Finite R (P.complex.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, d < i → IsZero (P.complex.X i))
